samples.summary: Cell-internal selection: a forward-affinity END now bumps `endLineIdx` to the next visual line, making the previous line's rect extend to the cell's right edge instead of stopping at the selected text
samples.evidence: `const endLineIdx = lineIdxForOffset(endCbiEff, end.offset, endAffinity);` (selection.ts:366) — previously the end was hard-coded 'backward'. When an endpoint carries an explicit `lineAffinity: 'forward'` (e.g. the user clicks the left margin of a wrapped continuation line inside a table cell — find-position-at-pixel.ts:116 returns 'forward' there — and then drags left/up so that click becomes the range END), `endLineIdx` becomes startLineIdx+1. The loop at selection.ts:424-436 then takes the `li === startLineIdx` branch and paints `lineWidth = cellRightX - startPixel.x`, i.e. all the way to the cell's right padding edge, plus a zero-width rect on the next line — even though nothing on the next line is selected. The paragraph path does not have this problem because it stops at `getLineEndX` (text end, selection.ts:503), so the two paths now disagree.

samples.summary: The caret affinity round-trip only works for mouse-derived positions; keyboard caret moves never put `lineAffinity` on `cursor.position`, so the comment's claim ("dropping it here would undo the anchor round-trip") does not hold for arrow/vertical moves
samples.evidence: `Cursor.moveTo` (packages/docs/src/view/cursor.ts:28-31) assigns `this.position = pos` and `this.lineAffinity = affinity` separately — the affinity argument is NOT written onto the stored position object. In `handleArrow` (text-editor.ts:2776-2780) the diff stamps the affinity only on the selection `focus` (`focus: { ...newPos, lineAffinity: focusAffinity }`) while `this.cursor.moveTo(newPos, focusAffinity)` passes the bare `newPos` from `moveLeft`/`moveRight`/`moveVertical` (text-editor.ts:3887, 3934, 4104), which return `{ blockId, offset }` with no affinity. `fireCursorMoveCallbacks(cursor.position, ...)` (editor.ts:1160/2069) therefore publishes a caret with no `lineAffinity`, `updateCursorPos` anchors none (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2999), and `restoreLocalCursor` falls back to `'backward'` — the caret still collapses onto the previous visual line after a remote edit when it was placed by shift/arrow keys at a wrap boundary. Only clicks (text-editor.ts:1521-1525) benefit.
searchedFor: grep fireCursorMoveCallbacks call sites in packages/docs/src/view
grep updateCursorPos call sites in packages/frontend/src

samples.summary: The public `onCursorMove` callback type still declares endpoints as `{ blockId; offset }`, so the presence pipeline's new `lineAffinity` travels only as an undeclared runtime property
samples.evidence: editor.ts:128 and the internal `CursorMoveCallback` alias at editor.ts:1179 type both `pos` and the selection endpoints as `{ blockId: string; offset: number }`. The frontend consumer (docs-view.tsx:399 `store.updateCursorPos(pos, sel)`) only works today because `fireCursorMoveCallbacks(cursor.position, selRange)` passes the objects by reference; any consumer that reconstructs the object from the declared type (as several call sites in text-editor.ts already do) silently drops the field, and nothing type-checks that away — `packages/frontend` has no `tsc` lane at all.

samples.summary: `handleHome` stamps `lineAffinity: 'forward'` on the shift-selection focus unconditionally, including when the visual line start is the block start (offset 0 on the first line), where the documented reading is 'backward'
samples.evidence: `focus: { ...newPos, lineAffinity: 'forward' }` (text-editor.ts:2813) — `getVisualLineStart` returns offset 0 when the caret is on the block's first visual line, and find-position-at-pixel.ts:116-117 states "The first line in a block has no prior boundary, so it's always 'backward'". The mismatch is inert today (findPageForPosition's forward branch requires `charCount + lineChars === offset`, i.e. an empty leading line), but the invariant that only continuation-line starts carry 'forward' is broken here, and the same value is fed to the caret at line 2818.

finding.summary: clampPosToModel swallows an unresolvable blockId, but the very next call (anchorDocPosition) rethrows it uncaught from updateCursorPos
finding.evidence: clampPosToModel (l.957-977, touched by this delta) wraps everything in try/catch and returns `pos` unchanged when the block cannot be resolved — resolveBlockTreePath throws `Block not found: ${blockId}` (l.867). updateCursorPos then immediately calls `this.anchorDocPosition(clampedPos, clampedPos.lineAffinity)` (l.2999) with that same unresolvable position, and anchorDocPosition has no try/catch and no `if (!block)` guard: l.925 resolveBlockTreePath throws, or if it does resolve, `getBlockByRegion` (typed `Block` but can return `undefined` at runtime, l.1383-1394) feeds `this.blockTextLength(block)` at l.928 → TypeError. anchorDocRange (l.994) has the same exposure for selection endpoints. So the defensive catch added in clampPosToModel is illusory: a caret referencing a block a remote peer just deleted still throws out of updateCursorPos, which is called from the editor's cursor-move path with no caller-side handling.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. resolveBlockTreePath throws `Block not found` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:867. clampPosToModel (:957-977) catches that and returns the position unchanged (its own comment at :954-955 says so), but updateCursorPos immediately re-resolves the same unresolvable position via anchorDocPosition (:2999) and anchorDocRange (:3001). anchorDocPosition (:916-941) has no try/catch and no `!block` guard — its only early return is for a missing tree (:922) — so :925 rethrows, and even on a resolve it calls blockTextLength(block) at :928 on getBlockByRegion's result, which is typed `Block` but returns `blocks[topIndex]` unchecked (:1383-1394), giving a TypeError. Callers do not handle it: docs-view.tsx:399 and the setTimeout at docs-view.tsx:405-409 call store.updateCursorPos bare from editor.onCursorMove, and the timer branch republishes a `pos` captured up to CURSOR_UPDATE_THROTTLE ms earlier, so a remote block deletion in that window throws uncaught from a timer. editor.validateCursorPosition() only runs in onRemoteChange (docs-view.tsx:379) and does not re-check the captured pos, so it is not a guard for this path. The defensive catch is therefore illusory, and this is a missing-guard/uncaught-throw correctness defect on a real path.
